$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.reason: User requested an internal-only editorial ranking (0-10) plus five internal vibe-tag checkboxes (Underground, Mainstream, Comercial, LGBTQIA+, Sex Party) on the event CPT, to let apollo-telegram (and, deliberately, any other Apollo plugin) query for 'the best/most precise event right now' without hand-rolling that logic per-consumer. Explicit requirement: NEVER rendered on any public/frontend surface.
$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.fix: Six new meta keys registered in apollo-core/src/Core/MetaRegistry.php under the `event` post type, all show_in_rest => false and auth_callback => manage_options: _event_int_rank (integer 0-10, sanitize_callback clamps range, default 0) and _event_tag_underground / _event_tag_mainstream / _event_tag_comercial / _event_tag_lgbtqia / _event_tag_sexparty (boolean, string '1'/'' storage, same convention as _event_is_gone / _event_highlighted). New file apollo-events/src/Admin/RankMetabox.php (own file, own concern, separate from Metabox.php) renders a 0-10 select plus the five checkboxes inside the Publish box on the wp-admin single-event editor, physically moved via inline JS to sit right below the Publish/Update button as requested. Visible and writable only under current_user_can('manage_options'), checked at render() AND save() AND a third time inside each setter helper (apollo_event_set_int_rank / apollo_event_set_tag) — defense in depth so a future programmatic caller can't bypass the gate by skipping the form.
$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.helpers: apollo-events/includes/functions.php gained: apollo_event_internal_tags() (the single canonical slug=>meta_key map — UI loop, save handler and every read helper all consume this one function so a new tag is added in exactly one place), apollo_event_internal_tag_labels(), apollo_event_get_int_rank()/set_int_rank(), apollo_event_get_tags()/is_tag()/set_tag(), apollo_event_get_top_ranked() (upcoming, non-expired events ordered by rank desc / soonest-first tiebreak), and apollo_event_find_best_match() — the generic plug-and-play entry point: takes optional tags[]/tags_mode/min_rank/loc_id/from/limit criteria and returns ready-to-use event payloads (id, title, permalink, rank, tags, start_date/time, loc, djs), folding rank + tags + date proximity + expiration exclusion into one call so ANY Apollo plugin can ask 'what event fits right now' without re-deriving the rule. All global-aliased in includes/functions-global.php so callers outside the Apollo\Event namespace (apollo-telegram included) can call them unprefixed.
$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.scope_decision: Same reasoning as _event_highlighted: these are editorial/internal signals an admin sets deliberately, not organizer-submitted data — absent from EventsController's REST meta_map and from the /novo-evento public form by design, and additionally unregistered from REST entirely (show_in_rest => false) so they cannot leak through the generic post-meta REST endpoint or the Gutenberg meta panel even in principle.
$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.data_registry: Added six full field-shape entries (event.int_rank, event.tag_underground, event.tag_mainstream, event.tag_comercial, event.tag_lgbtqia, event.tag_sexparty) to _inventory/data-registry.json, positioned right after the existing event.highlighted entry.
$int_rank_and_vibe_tags_2026_08_24.not_yet_done: No bulk backfill of existing events — apollo_event_get_int_rank()/get_tags() default absent meta to 0/false, so every already-published event reads as baseline/worst-rank with no tags until an admin opens it and sets values, matching the 'if not number gave that 0' requirement without a write storm across the table. apollo-telegram itself has not yet been wired to CALL apollo_event_find_best_match() — that consumer-side wiring is separate follow-up work; this note covers the meta field + helper plumbing only.

$highlighted_meta_field_2026_07_28.reason: User requested a curation flag so upcoming events can be surfaced in a dedicated hero slider on the Eventos screens (/casa teaser + the full /eventos page being prepped this same pass).
$highlighted_meta_field_2026_07_28.fix: New meta key _event_highlighted (string '1'/'', same convention as the pre-existing _event_is_gone), registered three places: (1) src/Registry.php register_meta() — apollo_core_register_meta filter, so it's part of the plugin's declared meta config; (2) src/Admin/Metabox.php render_config() — checkbox at the top of the '⚙ Configurações' side metabox, labelled '⭐ Destacar (Highlighted)'; (3) src/Admin/Metabox.php save() — same isset($_POST[...]) ? '1' : '' pattern as _event_is_gone.
$highlighted_meta_field_2026_07_28.scope_decision: Deliberately NOT added to EventsController's REST meta_map (the public-write path used by /novo-evento's frontend submit form) — this is an editorial curation flag an admin sets after the fact, not something an organizer self-selects when submitting their own event. Matches how _event_is_gone (a conceptually similar admin-only status flag) is already scoped: present in the admin metabox, absent from the REST meta_map.
$highlighted_meta_field_2026_07_28.data_registry: Added a full field-shape entry (id: event.highlighted) to _inventory/data-registry.json, positioned right after the existing event.is_gone entry, plus listed in the not_in_metabox audit array (accurate — it's covered by apollo-events' own native Metabox.php, not by apollo-lux-panels, which is what that specific audit array tracks).
$highlighted_meta_field_2026_07_28.not_yet_done: The actual hero-slider consumer (reading _event_highlighted to build the /eventos .pev-hero slider and the /casa hero) is separate follow-up work, tracked in this same session's task list — this note covers the meta field plumbing only.

$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.reason: User asked to refine 6 things on the live /eventos screen (luxury month arrows, month-switch slide animation, filter menu z-index/blur legibility, cap 'Ultimos eventos registrados' to 3 + lightbox, .pev-hero highlighted-events slider, day-window rails with infinite reveal). Investigation found the live archive-event.php was an older 'ev-*' radar-grid template that never had any .pev-* markup at all -- the refinements described code that didn't exist yet. Surfaced this to the user via AskUserQuestion; user chose 'Build the full .pev-* page now' -- i.e. build the whole Portal de Eventos (Netflix-style promoter calendar) screen for real, not just the 6 tweaks in isolation.
$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.source: Ported from screen/_official_layout/{simulated.data-portal.js, js/app-portal-eventos.js, css/portal-eventos.css} -- read in full and ported near-verbatim. Both JS files are generic (operate only on window.APOLLO_EVENTS + the DOM), so porting was a straight copy with real WP data standing in for the mockup's fixture array, not a rewrite. All 6 requested refinements were already fully designed in the mockup (including inline before/after doc comments explaining the exact luxury-arrow redesign and the filter-menu legibility fix), so this pass is fidelity-focused porting, not new design work.
$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.fix: archive-event.php rewritten: data section now builds $portal_events (one row per published event) shaped to match the mockup's APOLLO_EVENTS contract (id, title, cover, startDate, startTime, venue{name,address}, lineup[{name}], genres[], season, tickets, ticketsUrl, highlight, status, about, url). Body markup replaced with a single #apollo-portal-root mount point -- all DOM is built client-side by the ported JS, same as the mockup. Two new template-parts: portal-styles.php (portal-eventos.css ported verbatim, only the mockup's '#view-eventos' SPA router ID prefix dropped since this page has no router) and portal-scripts.php (window.APOLLO_EVENTS data injection + simulated.data-portal.js ported as portal-data.js + app-portal-eventos.js ported verbatim + a small DOMContentLoaded bootstrap replacing the mockup's view.eventos.js router glue). Old hero.php/toolbar.php/event-card.php/scripts.php/styles.php template-parts left on disk but no longer required by archive-event.php (superseded, not deleted, in case of rollback).
$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.highlighted_meta_wired: The .pev-hero slider's data source is APOLLO_PORTAL.highlights(), which the WP side feeds from the _event_highlighted meta added earlier this same session ('1' -> highlight:true in $portal_events) -- this closes the loop the previous note's not_yet_done flagged.
adaptations_from_mockup: season: real events have no hand-authored season tag like the mockup's demo fixtures (summer/winter/rockinrio/nye/carnival). PHP derives one from the event's calendar month using the same BR-seasons-rough heuristic portal-data.js's own seasonBanner() fallback already used (Dec-Feb summer, Mar-May outono, Jun-Aug winter, Sep-Nov primavera). SEASON_LABEL gained two entries (outono/primavera) to label the two buckets the mockup never needed.

tickets: mapped directly from the real _event_ticket_status meta (enum free|available|soldout_soon|sold_out, already existed in EventsController) -- exact 1:1 match with the mockup's tickets field, no adaptation needed.

'recent' rail sort: the mockup's recent() sorts by event startDate descending (furthest-future event first), which reads oddly against the Portuguese label 'Ultimos eventos registrados' (last REGISTERED). Not changed in the ported function (kept byte-identical) -- flagging here in case a future pass wants recent() to sort by post_date (creation order) instead to better match the label's literal meaning.

lineup: DJ start/end set times (_event_dj_slots, used by EventsController's REST enrichment) were not pulled in -- lineup entries carry name only. The modal's lineup list still renders correctly (times just render blank); can be added later if the per-slot schedule is wanted in the quick-view modal.

openModal() gained one extra action button vs the mockup: 'Ver pagina completa' linking to the real WP permalink (ev.url, a WP-only addition to the data shape). The mockup's modal is a dead end by design (demo data, nothing to navigate to); the live site still needs a path to the full single-event page.

CSS: appended a small WP-host-only block (not in the mockup) giving .pev-host top padding and offsetting .pev-chrome's sticky top -- the mockup assumes it's mounted inside the SPA's own app-shell layout; this page instead sits under the real fixed .ax-top bar rendered by apollo_get_navbar() -> apollo_render_app_shell(), so the portal needs to clear it. Values (78px / 64px) matched against shell-styles.php's live .ax-top-blur height (78px) and .ax-top position+height (2px + 56px = 58px bottom edge).
$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.not_touched: TemplateLoader.php routing is unchanged -- /eventos already resolved to styles/base/archive-event.php before this pass, so only the destination template's content changed, not the route. The .ax-aside/.nb sidebar nav flagged as a gap earlier this session (hidden comments in layout.html, tasks around the mandatory header) is still not built; this page renders through apollo_get_navbar() -> apollo_render_app_shell() same as before, so it will inherit the aside automatically whenever that shell component is eventually built -- no extra wiring needed here.
$portal_eventos_build_2026_07_28.verification: node --check run against the mockup's two original JS files (proving the verbatim-ported portions parse cleanly); grep-verified <script>/</script> and IIFE open/close pairing in the written portal-scripts.php; grep-verified no :root redeclaration in portal-styles.php (the mockup's own hard rule); grep-verified both deltas (SEASON_LABEL outono/primavera, 'Ver pagina completa' link) landed at the intended lines. Full node/php execution against the live plugin files was not possible this session -- apollo-events/ is outside the bash sandbox's mounted folders (only apollo-templates is mounted); verification relied on Read/Grep plus the mockup-file node --check proxy described above.

$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.remount: archive-event.php no longer owns a document. It used to call apollo_render_document_open(), print its own <body> and render its own navbar -- so /eventos had NO .ax-aside at all and duplicated shell logic. It is now a mount point on the Blank Canvas Apollo+ shell (apollo_plus_open/close), same as /feed in phase 001, with a legacy self-hosted-document fallback if apollo-templates is inactive so the archive can never hard-fail on a missing shell.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.routing_divergence_fixed: /portal and /portal/eventos mapped to 'dashboard' -- the LOGGED-IN promoter panel. Two dead code paths proved this was unintended: archive-event.php has always branched on apollo_event_page === 'portal' (a value neither route map could emit), and handle_virtual_pages() has always handled a 'portal_archive' value that was likewise unreachable. Net effect: the public portal could not be reached, while /portal quietly served the private panel. Both maps now send /portal + /portal/eventos to 'portal_archive'; the panel keeps /meus-eventos, /painel, /painel/eventos, /dashboard. The existing flush signature (md5 of version + route_map) picks the change up automatically on the next request.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.modularised: portal-styles.php (979 lines) split into portal/styles-{base,chrome,browse,hero,rails,modals,responsive}.php behind portal/styles.php; portal-scripts.php (1258 lines) split into portal/{data,helpers,app,bootstrap}.php behind portal/scripts.php. The CSS split was verified LOSSLESS by rejoining the seven parts and diffing against the original (26014 chars both sides, exact match) -- a split, not a restyle. Both original filenames survive as thin forwarders so theme overrides and stale include paths still resolve.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.shell_fit: The pre-split file hard-coded .pev-host{padding-top:78px} / .pev-chrome{top:64px} against the standalone navbar this screen used to render for itself. Re-derived against the real shell (.ax-top sits at top:2px, height 56px per shell-styles.php) and, at >=1000px, the portal's own 16px side padding is zeroed because .ax-main already supplies the gutters beside the pinned aside -- otherwise they doubled.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.BLOCKER_not_serving_this_file: VERIFICATION FAILED AND THE PHASE IS NOT CONFIRMED DONE. After deploy, /portal and /portal/eventos correctly resolve to the portal route (title and canonical are right, proving the routing fix landed), but the RENDERED BODY is the old 'ev-*' radar archive -- hero.php + toolbar.php + event-card.php + the ev-counter, plus the LEGACY navbar rather than .ax-top. No current version of archive-event.php renders that markup in either its Apollo+ or its fallback branch. apollo-templates changes ARE live (/feed now redirects guests to /acesso per phase 001), so RealTimeSync is working -- which means styles/base/archive-event.php is being SHADOWED, not un-synced.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.BLOCKER_cause_hypothesis: TemplateLoader::locate() resolves THEME-FIRST: wp-content/themes/{child|parent}/apollo-events/{style}/archive-event.php outranks the plugin file. Either (a) the active theme ships an override carrying the old markup, or (b) the active-style option points at a pack other than 'base' and a theme file exists for it. Both make plugin-side edits silently ineffective. Cannot be distinguished from here -- the server filesystem is not reachable from this session.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.diagnostic_added: archive-event.php now prints a provenance comment into the page source: '<!-- apollo-events {version} | template: styles/base/archive-event.php | style: {style} | portal: {page} -->'. If that comment is ABSENT from view-source on /portal, the plugin file is confirmed shadowed and the override must be removed or updated; if PRESENT, the problem is elsewhere and the marker reports the active style pack directly.
$phase_002_eventos_apollo_plus_2026_07_2.phase_status: Code complete and structurally verified (all 17 touched files balance; CSS split proven lossless). Runtime NOT verified. Phase 002 should not be considered closed until the provenance marker is observed on /portal.
files: styles/base/archive-event.php (re-mounted on Apollo+ shell + provenance marker)

$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.phase: 002 review — user-reported defects on the live portal
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.correction_to_previous_note: The $phase_002 note claimed styles/base/archive-event.php was being SHADOWED by a theme override. THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. The user confirmed the new portal is live ('Phase 2 reproved') and reported defects that only exist in the NEW screen. The reason my fetches kept returning the old markup is PAGE CACHE: two fetches ~2 minutes apart returned a byte-identical meta-apollo-csp-nonce (ANCLHEnNtILEY9RRkyEAeA==), which is per-request and cannot repeat on an uncached response. The provenance marker added in that pass stays -- it is still the fastest way to answer 'which template rendered' -- but the shadowing hypothesis is retracted.
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_1_collapsed_cards: REPORTED: 'collapsed event-card opened on page portal; listing events broken'. CAUSE: the portal stylesheet only ever shipped OVERRIDES scoped to .eve-grid.grid-layout, assuming the Design System's .a-eve-card component and .grid-layout grid were already loaded -- true in the mockup (ds-components.css + market.css are linked), false on WordPress, where .a-eve-card lives in apollo-templates/assets/css/event-card.css and .grid-layout existed only in mural.css. Neither is enqueued on a blank-canvas page (no wp_head()). With no base rules every card collapsed to text height. FIX: new portal/styles-cards.php INLINES event-card.css from its real file (so apollo-templates stays the single source of truth and edits there still reach this screen) and defines .grid-layout at component level (2-up mobile, 4-up >=1000px).
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_2_fake_highlight: REPORTED: 'event Dismantle 2 is highlighted true? I dont remember tagging as meta cpt event of highlight TRUE'. CORRECT -- they never did. CAUSE: highlights() was ported verbatim from the mockup, including its fallback: when NO event carries highlight:true it returns featured() -- the best-ranked event of the month -- and the hero then labels that event 'Destaque'. Harmless in a demo, a fabricated editorial claim on a real site. FIX: fallback removed. No _event_highlighted, no highlight. The hero renders an honest empty state ('Nenhum evento em destaque' + how to set one) instead of promoting an event nobody chose.
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_3_arrows: REPORTED: 'Arrows left right broken with wrong border, background, shadow'. TWO causes, both fixed. (a) styles-responsive.php still carried the PRE-redesign arrow rules -- .pev-month-btn--next{font-size:32px;translateX(8px)} / --prev{16px;-8px} -- the exact 'two raw arrows at different sizes with manual offsets' the luxury pill redesign replaced. They survived inside the >=1000px block and silently undid the redesign on desktop: mismatched glyphs shoved sideways inside a 34px pill. Removed; styles-chrome.php is now the single definition at every breakpoint. (b) The portal now renders inside the Apollo+ shell where the Design System's generic button rules apply and were bleeding border/background/box-shadow into the pills. styles-chrome.php now states the pill owns its surface (border:0!important, appearance:none) and neutralises the icon's inherited box + pointer-events.
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_4_disponivel_tag: REPORTED: 'TAG "DISPONIVEL" IS FIXED SIMULATED DATA OR CONNECTED TO PROPER CORRECT TAXONOMY SELECTED FROM event_tag + event_type + event_category?'. ANSWER: NEITHER -- and it was wrong. It came from the _event_ticket_status META (enum free|available|soldout_soon|sold_out), and archive-event.php read it as `?: 'available'`, so ANY event with no ticket status set silently rendered a 'Disponível' chip. Not simulated data, but a default that looked like data -- an availability claim the site had no basis for. FIX: the `?: 'available'` default is gone; empty status now stays empty and ticketChip()/ticketStatus() render nothing rather than inventing a label. SEPARATELY, the card's visible tag pills now come from the REAL editorial taxonomies: archive-event.php exposes a `tags` array merged from event_tag + event_type + event_category (human-assigned in wp-admin) and eveCardHTML() prefers it, falling back to the `sound` genre terms only when an event carries none of those -- also real terms, never a defaulted meta value.

$phase_002_ds_component_port_2026_07_28.severity: root-cause — supersedes the styles-cards.php fix from the previous pass

Because the class names matched, it looked like a fix; it was a substitution. That is why the listed events rendered with no background and why 'a ton of elements' were still wrong -- everything downstream of the card component was being styled by the wrong source.
$phase_002_ds_component_port_2026_07_28.method_correction: The instruction from the start was to replicate the mockup precisely. Patching symptoms against a lookalike stylesheet cannot converge on that no matter how many rounds it takes. The correct method -- now applied -- is to port the mockup's own CSS verbatim and let the portal's parts override only what is genuinely portal-specific.
$phase_002_ds_component_port_2026_07_28.fix: New portal/styles-ds.php ports ds-components.css VERBATIM (asserted programmatically: the entire source file is contained in the emitted <style> block), plus the .section-header/.section-title/.section-count block and the .grid-layout grid + its >=999px override, both lifted verbatim from market.css. This brings the real card: 450px .a-eve-media with var(--surface-hover) background, the mask/-webkit-mask corner-notch geometry, the layered inset box-shadow, .a-eve-date cutout, the squircle .a-eve-tag pills, and the .event-row/.date-box listing component. styles-cards.php is now a documented no-op; the cascade runs base -> ds -> chrome -> browse -> hero -> rails -> modals -> responsive, so the portal's own tuning (scoped to .eve-grid.grid-layout) still lands on top of the DS base rather than replacing it.
$phase_002_ds_component_port_2026_07_28.standing_rule: ds-components.css is copied, never authored. If the card must change it changes in the Design System and is re-copied here. Any future screen in phases 003-011 that renders DS components must port from screen/_official_layout/css/*, NOT from a same-named file elsewhere in the plugin tree -- apollo-templates ships several lookalikes that are not the handoff.
$phase_002_ds_component_port_2026_07_28.verification: Programmatic containment check that ds-components.css appears verbatim inside styles-ds.php, plus spot assertions for the seven marker rules (.a-eve-media 450px, --surface-hover, mask-repeat, .a-eve-tag, .date-box, .section-title, .grid-layout). Brace/paren balance across all 15 portal parts. Runtime rendering NOT verified from this session -- the host serves a cached copy to unauthenticated fetches (proven earlier by a repeated per-request CSP nonce), so visual confirmation needs a cache purge and a look by the user.

$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.severity: root-cause -- facts strip and venue (map + slider) invisible in the lightbox on /eventos and /portal
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.reported: Facts strip and venue/map appear stranded (present in the DOM, unreadable) directly under the hero when an event card opens in the lightbox, but render correctly on /evento/{slug}.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.root_cause: apollo-single-event.js's initAnim()/bindDjRail() create every ScrollTrigger (facts+panels reveal, hero parallax, footer parallax, word reveal, DJ rail pin, DJ cards) with no `scroller` option, so they all default to `scroller: window`. On the real page the window scrolls and they fire normally. Inside the lightbox the fragment mounts in `.ev-lb-scroll`, a native overflow-y:auto panel; the document is Lenis-locked and the window never moves, so those triggers can never resolve and the affected elements stay at their GSAP inline `opacity:0` forever. A second, independent gap made this invisible to the existing safety nets: bootstrap.php's unstrand() pass and the CSS floor in styles-lightbox.php both queried only the class `.ev-reveal`, which no single-event template actually applies -- the real reveal targets (.ev-fact, .ev-panel, [data-ev=access/about], .ev-spotify, .ev-gallery, .v-slider, .ev-map, .ev-vbody, .ev-dj) are a separate, hardcoded selector list inline in the JS, so both nets matched zero nodes and were dead code for this exact symptom.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.fix: (A) Instance now resolves `this.scroller = root.closest('.ev-lb-scroll') || undefined` once at construction and passes `scroller: self.scroller` to all 6 ScrollTrigger configs; undefined on /evento/{slug} and inline embeds, so behaviour there is unchanged, byte for byte. (B) Widened bootstrap.php's unstrand() query and styles-lightbox.php's CSS floor to the same selector list initAnim() actually reveals, as a belt-and-braces layer for anything that still slips through (e.g. a late image reflow). Selector is duplicated by hand in three places (apollo-single-event.js, bootstrap.php, styles-lightbox.php) -- keep them in sync if the reveal list changes.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.why_not_scrollerProxy_alone: bootstrap.php already registers `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy('.ev-lb-scroll', {...})`, but a proxy only supplies custom get/set methods for a scroller identifier -- it does not retroactively re-target ScrollTriggers that were created with `scroller: window` (the default). Every trigger must still be told `scroller: panel` explicitly at creation time, which is exactly what was missing.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.verification: Structural: confirmed via grep that no template-part applies class `ev-reveal` to any node (facts.php inspected directly); confirmed apollo-single-event.js had exactly 6 scrollTrigger call sites, all now carrying `scroller: self.scroller`. Live /eventos + /portal lightbox check pending -- Claude in Chrome was not connected this session (see BLOCKERS chapter note); handed to the user to confirm the facts strip and venue section are no longer stranded on next open.

$reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.scope: The shared lightbox — every surface, not just events. Version bump 1.7.1 -> 1.7.2.
$reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.requirement: The surface behind a fragment is solid #fff, always, in both themes. Never a token that can flip, never rgba with alpha, never a blur that lets the page behind read through. A close control is always present.

defect_1_panel_was_not_white.effect: In dark mode the reader panel rendered #0b0b0d — near black. The requirement had been silently violated on every dark-theme install since the lightbox shipped.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.the_trap: Pinning `background` alone produces WHITE TEXT ON WHITE, because --ev-ink inverts independently of --ev-bg. That renders as a blank panel with a working close button — visually identical to the 2026-08-07 stale-asset failure and considerably harder to diagnose a second time. The whole local --ev-* block has to be pinned together or not at all.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.fix: portal/styles-lightbox.php pins --ev-bg/--ev-ink/--ev-mute/--ev-faint/--ev-line/--ev-line2/--ev-soft to their resolved light-theme literals and sets background:#fff on .ev-lb-panel. Component-scoped custom properties, the form the DS blesses — NOT a :root entry.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.ownership: styles-lightbox.php is now the DECLARED LAST-WORD OWNER of the reader surface colour (.ev-lb-panel background + token pin, .ev-lb-bd background). The base sheet keeps its own values as the standalone-page default and is out-specified by the doubled selector. Do not edit both — that is the cardinal sin.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.trade_off_accepted: Dark-mode readers get a light document panel. Deliberate: the fragment is a document, not chrome.

$reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.defect_2_backdrop_had_alpha: `.ev-lb-bd` was rgba(var(--rgb-diff),.72). The comment above it claimed nothing shows through a full-bleed panel — true once open, false for the ~520ms the panel is still transitioning from opacity:0, during which the backdrop IS the surface. Now an opaque #fff literal with backdrop-filter:none.

defect_3_nested_css_comment.what: :root { --ev-max: 440px }  followed by an inline /* … */ annotation INSIDE an already-open comment block. CSS comments do not nest, so the outer block terminated at that inner close.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.effect: A .ev-wrap width rule and fourteen lines of English prose were handed to the CSS parser as source. The .ev-wrap rule escaped unscoped into the global cascade — reaching the real /evento/{slug} page, not just the lightbox — and the prose survived only on the parser's silent error recovery.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.why_it_survived: Syntax highlighters DO nest comments; browsers do not. It read as a comment in every editor for months. That gap is why assertion E24 is mechanical rather than a review note.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.fix: Inner annotation rewritten without comment syntax. E24 now scans every styles*.php cell in the portal directory for a second opener inside an open span.

feature_fragment_hydration.problem: innerHTML never executes <script>. For events that was correct and documented — the event fragment's only script is an inert application/json config block and its behaviour comes from ApolloEventSingle.mount(). It stopped being the whole story the moment a second surface existed: apollo-djs ships its runtime as an inline IIFE in its `scripts` cell, and that cell is GENERATED by _sandbox/build-dj-cells.py with a do-not-hand-edit banner. A DJ fragment therefore injected as correct but DEAD html — no dock, no reveals, no shares, no scroll progress.
feature_fragment_hydration.rejected_design: A per-surface mount() API. It would have required hand-editing exactly the generated cell that must not be hand-edited, once per surface, forever.
feature_fragment_hydration.shipped: hydrateScripts() in assets/js/apollo-event-lightbox.js re-creates the fragment's own <script> nodes so the browser executes them. Zero per-plugin work, works for every surface that will ever be registered.
safety: Order preserved; a src= script blocks the ones after it, re-creating the guarantee a parsed document gives for free.
state.injectToken generation counter — a superseded fragment's async chain detects it lost and stands down, so two fast opens cannot interleave two runtimes.
EXECUTABLE allow-list — application/json and application/ld+json are data and are left alone.
Per-script failure containment; a detached node is skipped rather than aborting the chain.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: document-level listeners bound by a fragment runtime outlive the panel, because unmountCurrent() removes their targets but not the listeners. Their selector lookups then resolve to null and the handlers no-op. Revisit if a surface ever binds something with side effects that survive its own DOM.
feature_fragment_hydration.event_path_untouched: ApolloEventSingle.mount() still runs exactly as before. Hydration is a no-op for events.
